summary.intent: Fix intermittent Windows desktop e2e CI failures during the build step, and open a PR for a previously completed docs update.
summary.outcome: Docs PR #502 was opened and merged. A root-cause fix was implemented across all 5 shared packages (crypto, core, api-client, sdk-core, sdk): tsup's unreliable concurrent dts worker was replaced with a deterministic post-build `tsc --emitDeclarationOnly` step, verified locally against all consumers including the exact failing CI step.

repo: All 5 shared packages (crypto, core, api-client, sdk-core, sdk) used an identical `"build": "tsup"` script with `dts: true, clean: true` in tsup config — a single pattern to fix universally.

The CI workflow builds packages sequentially without turbo; 'Build desktop frontend' runs tsup for core/sdk-core before 'Build API' runs nest build, so a silent tsup dts failure manifests only in the downstream API step.
tsconfig.base.json already sets `declaration: true, noEmit: false`, so per-package tsconfig.build.json only needs `emitDeclarationOnly: true` plus test-file excludes.
The `packages/crypto` package is special: it has two tsup config objects and uses `noExternal: [/.*/]` to bundle all deps — noted as a potential edge case for dts emit behavior.
The root `typecheck` script builds all 5 packages then runs `tsc -b` on the web app, making it a reliable end-to-end consumer validation.
The `intel/` directory is an untracked placeholder that appears as an uncommitted change warning but is expected and excluded from commits.

code.finding: Had two config objects and `noExternal: [/.*/]` — unique among the 5 packages; `dts` set to false as part of fix.
`dts: true, clean: true` caused silent Windows dts emission failure — tsup exits 0 even when .d.ts not written.
Build script was `"build": "tsup"` — changed to `"build": "tsup && tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --emitDeclarationOnly --declaration --outDir dist"` across all 5 packages.

workflow: tsup with `dts: true` runs declaration emit as a separate concurrent rollup-dts worker pass; on Windows, file locking or antivirus scanning can cause it to silently fail to emit .d.ts while still exiting 0.
The pattern of 'fails then passes on rerun' is a strong signal of a silent non-zero artifact from a parallel build worker, not a timing/race condition in tests.
Replacing tsup dts with `tsc --emitDeclarationOnly` run sequentially after tsup makes declaration failure deterministic (non-zero exit) rather than silent.
CI job annotations (visible before the full log is downloadable) were sufficient to identify the root cause module and error type without waiting for the full log.
Building packages in dependency order locally (crypto → core → api-client → sdk-core → sdk → api nest build) replicates the exact CI failure scenario for verification.

friction: Full CI job log was not downloadable while the rerun was still in progress, requiring diagnosis from annotations alone.
tsup's silent-success behavior on Windows dts failure made the bug look like test flakiness rather than a build correctness issue.
open_items: The fix is committed locally but the PR to merge the fix branch has not been opened yet — the transcript ends at the commit step.
The `intel/` untracked placeholder directory was noted but intentionally left out of the commit — its purpose and cleanup are unresolved.

Cheaper symptom-only alternatives were identified (CI guard checking for .d.ts existence, retry action) but not implemented — may be worth adding as a belt-and-suspenders safeguard even with the fix in place.
